title: DashboardOperational
wrapsNative: NavigationStack with navigationTitle and a toolbar (a Menu holding a Picker for the period, a Toggle for arrange mode), ScrollView, LazyVGrid of MonarchStatCard for the figures, MonarchInsightStrip, and MonarchDashboardGrid of MonarchWidget, MonarchLineChart, MonarchLeaderboard and MonarchActivityTimeline sections; LabeledContent with .labeledContentStyle(.monarch) for list rows
summary: A recipe, not a component: the home screen of an operational product, with an optional notice, key figures, insights and a grid of sections for status, what needs attention, the person's queue, a trend, team load, what is coming up and recent activity.
whenToUse: For the first screen of a product that watches live work, such as a support desk or a service-status tool, where people check what needs action now. On iPad the same grid shows two or three columns.
whenNotToUse: For a product built around stages (deals, candidates, campaigns), use the dashboard-pipeline recipe. For a single chart or list, put a MonarchWidget on the screen without the grid.
api: NavigationStack { ScrollView { VStack { MonarchBanner(_:message:tone:actionTitle:action:); LazyVGrid(columns:spacing:) { MonarchStatCard(…) }; MonarchInsightStrip(_:insights:); MonarchDashboardGrid(_:layout:itemLabel:span:isEditing:labels:content:) } }.navigationTitle(_:).toolbar { … } }

MonarchDashboardGrid content: MonarchWidget(_:systemImage:onViewAll:content:) for status, attention, queue and upcoming; MonarchLineChart(_:categories:series:description:) for the trend; MonarchWidget { MonarchLeaderboard(_:label:valueLabel:sort:isCompact:) } for team load; the activity-widget recipe for recent activity
.toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .primaryAction) { Menu { Picker("Period", selection:content:) } label: { … } }; ToolbarItem(placement: .secondaryAction) { Toggle(_:systemImage:isOn:) } }

options.name: sections
options.type: An Identifiable enum of the app's sections
options.description: One case per section, with a title for the grid's labels and a MonarchDashboardGridSpan for wide screens (status full width, attention and trend two columns, the rest one). Leave a case out and the grid closes up.

options.name: layout
options.description: The person's saved order of section ids, passed to MonarchDashboardGrid; empty keeps the default order. Store it per person.

options.name: isEditing
options.description: Arrange mode, from the toolbar toggle: each section gets move buttons.

options.name: period
options.description: The period chosen in the toolbar menu; the app reloads the figures and sections for it.

options.name: notice
options.description: A full-width note above the figures, such as a setup step.

states.name: phone
states.description: One column: the figures two across (one across at accessibility text sizes), the insights, then each section full width in the saved order.

states.name: iPad
states.description: From 640 points of grid width MonarchDashboardGrid shows two columns and from the wide breakpoint three; sections keep their spans.

states.name: arrange
states.description: With the Arrange toggle on, MonarchDashboardGrid shows move buttons on each section and reports the new order through layout.

states.name: loading
states.description: MonarchStatCard with isLoading shows placeholder figures; each MonarchWidget with state .loading and each chart with status .loading keeps its height.

states.name: empty
states.description: A section with nothing to show uses MonarchWidget state .empty with its own message, for example "Nothing needs attention right now."

states.name: error
states.description: A section that failed uses MonarchWidget state .failed with Try again; the rest of the screen stays usable.

appearance: The canvas is the screen background; figures, sections and charts are Monarch cards on the surface colour with their own borders, the notice uses the info tone and the status badges and attention badges use their tone colours with an icon. The navigation bar and toolbar are the system ones; every part follows light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ships DashboardOperational as one component with section slots (status, attention, queue, trend, workload, upcoming, activity), a header with scope, period and actions, a KPIRow, an InsightStrip and a DashboardGrid. On iOS it is a recipe: the title goes to the navigation bar, the period becomes a Picker in a toolbar Menu and the actions toolbar items, and the app lists its sections as an enum for MonarchDashboardGrid, which is one column on a phone. A chart section is the chart itself, because the chart frame is already a card; wrapping it in MonarchWidget would draw a card in a card. The web's scope switcher is another toolbar Menu, its footer is content after the grid, and its headingLevel has no equivalent because navigation titles and section headings are set by the system. Android has no entry for this template yet.
accessibility: The screen title is the navigation bar title, which VoiceOver reads as the screen's heading; each section's title is a heading from MonarchWidget or the chart frame.
The figures are a group named "Key figures" and each MonarchStatCard is read as its label, value and change, with the change direction spoken, not shown by colour alone.
MonarchDashboardGrid is named "Dashboard sections"; in arrange mode each section has Move earlier and Move later buttons and custom actions, and each move is announced with the new position.
Period and Arrange are toolbar controls with text labels; Arrange is a toggle, so VoiceOver reads its state.
At accessibility text sizes the figures fall back to one column, and the grid is one column on a phone at every size.
edgeCases: With no sections, leave MonarchDashboardGrid out and show MonarchEmptyState instead of an empty grid.
A saved layout that names a section the app no longer shows is ignored by MonarchDashboardGrid; new sections are added at the end.
Long section titles wrap in MonarchWidget; long row labels wrap in LabeledContent.
Pull to refresh is .refreshable on the ScrollView when the app reloads every section at once.
